role: Assistant Director, Environmental Protection & Improvement, USDA Forest Service Northeastern Area
stance_basis: letter recommending vegetation in median and requesting tree-loss description before evaluating environmental impact
summary: Alfred H. Troutt, writing on behalf of the USDA Forest Service Northeastern Area, reviewed the Lincoln Highway mobility study and raised concerns about vegetation, tree loss from right-of-way widening, and potential drainage issues at the western section. He expressed conditional support, suggesting specific improvements (trees/shrubs in median for soil retention and noise barriers) and requesting additional information on tree losses to facilitate environmental impact evaluation.
complaint_summary: Troutt raises concerns about the loss of woodland and vegetation, recommends trees and shrubs in the median strip for soil retention, traffic distraction prevention, and noise barriers, requests a description of tree losses from right-of-way widening to evaluate environmental impact, and notes potential water trapping drainage issues at the western section.

statement.text:
We have reviewed the Mobility Studies description for Section 4(f) lands - F.A. Route 23 (U.S. Route 30), Lincoln Highway (Chicago Avenue to Cicero Avenue) Cook County, Illinois.
Our interest in the project is in the effect on woodland and other vegetation, and largely coincides with that of the Cook County Forest Preserve District, with whom you have been working. A few trees and shrubs in the median strip would hold the soil and also prevent distraction between eastbound and westbound traffic. Trees can also be used as a noise barrier where needed.
According to the document, most of the route will be through business and residential property. The residential properties, at least, undoubtedly have some trees. A description of the losses of trees, resulting from the increase of the width of the right of way, would facilitate evaluation of environmental impact.
Some water may be trapped behind the slight slopes on both sides of the road at the western section (Exhibit "B") unless provisions are made for drainage of the low spots.
Thank you for the opportunity to comment on this highway project.
